applicability: Applies to the stated family: a nonempty set of 1-10 distinct decimal digits and an integer max_length in 1..4, counting distinct primes formable from up to max_length chosen digits without repetition and with no leading zero. Inputs outside this domain (duplicate or out-of-range digits, non-integer or boolean values, max_length outside 1..4) are rejected with ValueError. It does not handle repeated digits, lengths above 4, or non-decimal bases.
description: Exhaustively enumerate all ordered selections of k distinct digits for k from 1 to min(max_length, number of distinct digits). Skip leading-zero multi-digit numbers. For single digits accept only 2,3,5,7. For longer numbers require the last digit in {1,3,7,9} and digit sum not divisible by 3, then confirm primality by exact trial division up to floor(sqrt(n)). Results are collected in a set to guarantee distinctness and the count is returned as a string. The method is exact; runtime is bounded by the small permutation space (at most 10 digits, max_length 4).
